title: What does your agent do when the Company says no?
checkedAgainst: the Personal Agent Protocol draft 1.0 (in progress; as published on 2026-11-13), read and not run: `model.test.ts` holds the model to section 7's error table and the rules of sections 3.3, 3.4, 4.4, 4.5, 4.7, 5.3, 5.5 and 5.6, and 1.0's rule in 8.13 that an error code the agent does not recognize is handled by its status, each test naming its section, and `answers.ts` computes the answers below from the model. There is no reference implementation here to run the model against. It is also held to what the protocol itself publishes, copied on 2026-11-13 into `fixtures/poppy-official.json`: every error the model sends in a JSON body passes the Company kit's error schema, and its extension_required and version_unsupported bodies are spec.md's examples.

answer: Each refusal’s code names its own remedy, and the agent applies that one: the wrong one loops, or throws away a good token

questions.question: Your agent's exchange comes back 400 invalid_session because its delegation has expired. What does it do, and why not start a new Session?
questions.answer: It stops sending the exchange and fixes the cause: a new delegation, in the same Session, so the cart is kept. A new Session would carry the same broken header and get 400 invalid_session again.

questions.question: Why are Session errors 400 rather than 401? What would go wrong if session_ended were a 401?
questions.answer: An OAuth library treats a 401 as a bad access token, so it would throw away a valid token, and the agent would refresh or ask you again for nothing. With 400 the library keeps the token.

questions.question: After session_ended, the agent starts a new Session and sends the exchange again, and that also gets session_ended. What now, and what did the new Session cost?
questions.answer: It stops sending the exchange: the new Session got session_ended too, and the agent sends again once. The first Session’s cart did not carry over.

questions.question: The agent calls the MCP server with its everyday token and gets 401 invalid_token with a resource_metadata URL. What does it do?
questions.answer: It reads the metadata, refreshes for a token with resource https://mcp.example.com/mcp, and uses that token only at the MCP server. Its everyday token keeps working at the API.

questions.question: You signed out of example.com yesterday. Today the agent's exchange gets a 401 with no error code, naming orders:write. Does it ask you to sign in?
questions.answer: No. A 401 with no code is handled as insufficient_scope, and after you sign out the agent continues signed out: it asks you to sign in again only if you ask it to.

steps.title: Turned back at the counter
steps.line: Predict: what should your agent do next?
steps.caption: Your agent sends the jacket exchange from chapter 1, with its seal and its key. This morning the Company turns the ticket back with a slip: 401 invalid_token, about the key. The key expired overnight. The agent could send it again, start a new Session, or ask you to sign in. Which would you do? The slip already says.
steps.picture: One lane runs from the agent to the Company’s counter. The agent holds its seal and a key for orders:read and orders:write. The agent sent the exchange after this: its access token expired. The ticket, with its seal, its key and a tag reading version 1.0, stands before a barrier, and the Company handed back a slip: 401 invalid_token, about the key; a leader from the slip rings the key. The agent has not answered yet. The remedy rail is idle: which remedy fits is for you to predict. The Company knows Session Yx2b7Q, whose cart holds the medium.

steps.title: The slip says what to bring
steps.line: invalid_token: refresh the key, send it again.
steps.caption: The agent trades its refresh token for a new access token, without asking you, and sends the same request: 200, the exchange is made. Each refusal’s code names its own remedy, and the agent applies that one: the wrong one loops, or throws away a good token. Had you disconnected the agent from your account, the refresh would fail, and the agent would carry on signed out.
steps.picture: One lane runs from the agent to the Company’s counter. The agent holds its seal and a key for orders:read and orders:write. After this: its access token expired, the exchange was refused with 401 invalid_token; the slip still points at the key. The agent answered with Refresh and sent it again: 200; the ticket rests docked at its stop. On the remedy rail, Refresh is lit and Sign in is struck through: Sign in would fail, because the refresh token still covers what the exchange needs, so the agent refreshes without asking you. The Company knows Session Yx2b7Q, whose cart holds the medium.

steps.title: A key cut for reading
steps.line: 403 names the scope; you approve it again.
steps.caption: Suppose you had approved only orders:read. The slip says 403 insufficient_scope, naming orders:write. A refresh gives no more than you approved, so the agent asks you to sign in again, for orders:read and orders:write together. A 401 with no code, sent with no key at all, is handled the same way, unless you signed out: then the agent waits for you to ask.
steps.picture: One lane runs from the agent to the Company’s counter. The agent holds its seal and a key for orders:read and orders:write. After this: you had approved only orders:read, the exchange was refused with 403 insufficient_scope; the slip still points at the key. The agent answered with Sign in and sent it again: 200; the ticket rests docked at its stop. On the remedy rail, Sign in is lit and Refresh is struck through: Refresh would fail, because the refresh token covers only orders:read, and a refresh cannot add orders:write, so the agent asks you. The Company knows Session Yx2b7Q, whose cart holds the medium.

steps.title: When the seal itself is wrong
steps.line: 400 invalid_session: fix the cause. A new Session won’t.
steps.caption: Now the number changes. The delegation that vouches for the agent’s signing key has expired, and the slip says 400 invalid_session, about the seal. A new Session would carry the same broken seal and be refused the same way. So the agent stops, gets a new delegation, signs again in the same Session, and sends. The cart is still there.
steps.picture: One lane runs from the agent to the Company’s counter. The agent holds its seal and a key for orders:read and orders:write. After this: the delegation behind its seal expired, the exchange was refused with 400 invalid_session; the slip still points at the seal. The agent answered with Re-sign and sent it again: 200; the ticket rests docked at its stop. On the remedy rail, Re-sign is lit and New Session is struck through: New Session would fail, because a new Session does not fix invalid_session: the same header fails in any Session, so the agent stops and fixes the cause. The Company knows Session Yx2b7Q, whose cart holds the medium.

steps.title: Why a seal’s error is not a 401
steps.line: A 401 would make OAuth code discard a good key.
steps.caption: OAuth libraries read a 401 as “this token is bad” and throw the token away. Had the Company answered the expired delegation with 401, the agent’s library would have discarded a key that was fine, and the agent would have refreshed, or asked you to sign in, for nothing. Poppy sends Session errors as 400, so the key stays where it is.
steps.picture: One lane runs from the agent to the Company’s counter. The agent holds its seal and a key for orders:read and orders:write. After this: the delegation behind its seal expired, the exchange was refused with 400 invalid_session; the slip still points at the seal. The agent answered with Re-sign and sent it again: 200; the ticket rests docked at its stop. On the remedy rail, Re-sign is lit and New Session is struck through: New Session would fail, because a new Session does not fix invalid_session: the same header fails in any Session, so the agent stops and fixes the cause. The Company knows Session Yx2b7Q, whose cart holds the medium. Beside it: an OAuth library keeps the key on a 400, and would throw a good key away on a 401.

steps.title: The Session is over
steps.line: session_ended: a new Session, and one more try.
steps.caption: The Company has ended the Session the cart was in. The slip says 400 session_ended, so the agent starts a new Session and sends the exchange again, once. The cart stays behind with the old Session. Had the new Session been refused the same way, the agent would have stopped there: without that rule, agent and Company could pass the request back and forth for ever.
steps.picture: One lane runs from the agent to the Company’s counter. The agent holds its seal and a key for orders:read and orders:write. After this: the Company ended the Session, the exchange was refused with 400 session_ended; the slip still points at the seal. The agent answered with New Session and sent it again: 200; the ticket rests docked at its stop. On the remedy rail, New Session is lit and Refresh is struck through: Refresh would fail, because session_ended is a 400: the access token is fine, so the agent keeps it. The Company knows Session a new one, whose cart is empty: the old cart stayed with the old Session.

steps.title: Same 400, a different move
steps.line: version_unsupported: read poppy.json again, then choose.
steps.caption: Third 400, third remedy. The agent used an old copy of poppy.json and sent version 0.4, which the Company no longer serves. It fetches poppy.json again, uncached, chooses 1.0, and, since a Session keeps one version, starts a new Session and sends once more. The extensions a request declares work the same way: a 403 extension_required names the one missing. Read the code, not just the number.
steps.picture: One lane runs from the agent to the Company’s counter. The agent holds its seal and a key for orders:read and orders:write. After this: it used an old copy of poppy.json and sent version 0.4, the exchange was refused with 400 version_unsupported; the slip still points at the version. The agent answered with Re-read and sent it again: 200; the ticket rests docked at its stop. On the remedy rail, Re-read is lit and New Session is struck through: New Session would fail, because version_unsupported asks for a fresh copy of poppy.json first; a new Session follows only if the agent then chooses another version. The Company knows Session a new one, whose cart is empty: the old cart stayed with the old Session.

steps.title: A key cut for one door
steps.line: The MCP server takes only keys issued for it.
steps.caption: A Company can list two kinds of API: an OpenAPI service and an MCP server. Both take the seal and the key. This MCP server accepts only tokens issued for it, so the everyday key comes back 401 invalid_token, with a link to the server’s metadata. The agent refreshes for a token whose resource is the server’s URL, and uses that token there and nowhere else.
steps.picture: Two lanes run from the agent to the Company’s counter: the API, idle, and the MCP server’s, in use. The agent holds its seal and a key for orders:read and orders:write, and a second key, cut for the MCP server only. After this: it asked the MCP server with its everyday key, the sizing call was refused with 401 invalid_token; the slip still points at the key. The agent answered with Refresh and sent it again: 200; the ticket rests docked at its stop. On the remedy rail, Refresh is lit and Sign in is struck through: Sign in would fail, because the refresh token still covers what the sizing call needs, so the agent refreshes without asking you. The Company knows Session a new one, whose cart is empty: the old cart stayed with the old Session.

steps.title: Slow down, then break it yourself
steps.line: Break the errand, then predict how the agent answers.
steps.caption: Send too fast and the Company answers 429 with Retry-After: 30. The key and the seal are fine, so the agent waits at least 30 seconds and sends the same request. Now it is yours. Break the errand one of seven ways, say which remedy you expect, then press Agent answers. The rail shows the remedy, and why the tempting one, New Session here, would fail.
steps.picture: One lane runs from the agent to the Company’s counter. The agent holds its seal and a key for orders:read and orders:write, and a second key, cut for the MCP server only. After this: it sent too many requests too fast, the exchange was refused with 429; the slip still points at the pace. The agent answered with Wait and sent it again: 200; the ticket rests docked at its stop. On the remedy rail, Wait is lit and New Session is struck through: New Session would fail, because 429 says the agent is sending too often; it waits at least 30 s and sends the same request. The Company knows Session a new one, whose cart is empty: the old cart stayed with the old Session.
